title: Taxis and Rides
goal: Arrange a ride, give a destination, confirm pickup details, and handle a change or missing item.

runs.text: Cab
and
taxi
are related words for a hired vehicle with a driver. A
taxi stand
is a waiting area. A
pickup location
is where the ride starts; a
drop-off location
is where you leave the vehicle.
Rideshare
here means an app-arranged ride. Ask about the particular service's arrangements.

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: Hi, I'd like to reserve a taxi for tomorrow morning.

turns.en: Hi, I'd like to reserve a taxi for tomorrow morning.

turns.speaker: Dispatcher

runs.text: Where should we pick you up?

turns.en: Where should we pick you up?

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: At the north entrance of Cedar Hotel, at 7:30.

turns.en: At the north entrance of Cedar Hotel, at 7:30.

turns.speaker: Dispatcher

runs.text: Where are you going?

turns.en: Where are you going?

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: The airport. There are four passengers and two large suitcases.

turns.en: The airport. There are four passengers and two large suitcases.

turns.speaker: Dispatcher

runs.text: I'll check which vehicle is available.

turns.en: I'll check which vehicle is available.

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: I'm also traveling with a service dog. Could you confirm the pickup arrangements?

turns.en: I'm also traveling with a service dog. Could you confirm the pickup arrangements?

turns.speaker: Dispatcher

runs.text: I'll note that and confirm the details with you.

turns.en: I'll note that and confirm the details with you.

runs.text: A
service dog

is a dog trained to perform tasks related to a person's disability. Ask clearly for arrangements you need. “Could you repeat the pickup time?” helps verify a booking. The answer may be a confirmation, or “We don't have a vehicle available then.” You can ask “What's the earliest time you can offer?”

turns.speaker: Passenger

runs.text: Are you the driver for Maya?

turns.en: Are you the driver for Maya?

turns.speaker: Driver

runs.text: Yes. You're going to Cedar Hotel?

turns.en: Yes. You're going to Cedar Hotel?

turns.speaker: Passenger

runs.text: That's right—the north entrance, please.

turns.en: That's right—the north entrance, please.

turns.speaker: Driver

runs.text: Do you have any bags for the trunk?

turns.en: Do you have any bags for the trunk?

turns.speaker: Passenger

runs.text: Just this suitcase.

turns.en: Just this suitcase.

blocks.caption: Get into the right trip · Passenger & Driver

runs.text: Trunk

is the storage area at the back of a car. “Can you take me to this address?” works when you can show the destination. “About how long will it take?” asks for an estimate, not a guarantee. “Does that estimate include tolls?” checks whether a charge is part of the quoted amount.

study.title: Change, pay, and recover an item

turns.speaker: Passenger

runs.text: Could we make one extra stop at the pharmacy?

turns.en: Could we make one extra stop at the pharmacy?

turns.speaker: Driver

runs.text: Possibly. It may change the fare. Which pharmacy?

turns.en: Possibly. It may change the fare. Which pharmacy?

turns.speaker: Passenger

runs.text: The one on Cedar Avenue. Could you tell me the additional cost first?

turns.en: The one on Cedar Avenue. Could you tell me the additional cost first?

blocks.caption: Change, pay, and recover an item · Passenger & Driver

runs.text: At the end: “Could you drop me off at this entrance?” “Can I pay by card?” “Could I have a receipt?”
Keep the change
tells someone not to return the difference from a cash payment. It is a choice in an appropriate payment situation, not a compulsory phrase or tipping rule.

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: I think I left my laptop in a taxi this morning.

turns.en: I think I left my laptop in a taxi this morning.

turns.speaker: Agent

runs.text: What time was the trip, and where did it end?

turns.en: What time was the trip, and where did it end?

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: Around eight. I went from Cedar Hotel to the airport.

turns.en: Around eight. I went from Cedar Hotel to the airport.

turns.speaker: Agent

runs.text: Do you have the trip reference?

turns.en: Do you have the trip reference?

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: Yes, it's on my receipt. What's the next step?

turns.en: Yes, it's on my receipt. What's the next step?

blocks.caption: Change, pay, and recover an item · Customer & Agent

runs.text: “I can't find the pickup area” and “I've been waiting twenty minutes” report a practical problem. “I need an update, please” is firm without pretending that a reply time is guaranteed.
Fictional trip: Maya, Cedar Hotel north entrance, tomorrow 7:30 a.m., airport, four passengers, two suitcases. Later problem: laptop missing after the ride.
Reserve the ride. Partner asks for pickup, destination, people, and bags. Confirm the essentials.
Partner says the driver is at the south entrance. Clarify your location and ask what to do.
Add a pharmacy stop. Partner says it may cost more. Ask for the amount before agreeing.
Report the missing laptop using the trip details.
Solo: read the dispatcher or driver turns and supply your own replies. Later change the pickup time and baggage.
Possibilities:

“I'm at the north entrance, not the south entrance.” “What would the total fare be?” “I think I left a laptop in the car.” Check that the listener can identify the ride, requested change, and unresolved problem.

ja: 乗車の確認と、行き先の変更。
note: 予約名、迎えの場所、行き先で乗車を確認します。途中の立ち寄りや忘れ物には、場所と時刻を添えます。
